questions.q: What two questions define the four categories in this lesson's 2x2 map?
options: Is it an asset or a liability, and is it current or long-term?
Is it revenue or expense, and has cash already moved or not yet?
Is it debit-normal or credit-normal, and is it a simple or compound entry?
Is it domestic or foreign currency, and is it taxable or non-taxable?
questions.explain: The four categories (accrued revenue, deferred revenue, accrued expense, deferred expense) come from crossing revenue-vs-expense with whether cash has moved yet.

questions.q: A customer pays $12,000 upfront for a year of subscription service that hasn't been delivered yet. Which category does this fall into?
questions.explain: Cash has already been collected, but the revenue has not yet been earned — this is Deferred (Unearned) Revenue.

questions.q: Employees earn wages in March that won't be paid until the April payroll run. Which category does this fall into?
questions.explain: The expense was incurred in March, but cash hasn't moved yet — this is an Accrued Expense.

questions.q: Oakmere Design Studio pays $12,000 on January 1 for a full year of insurance. What is the January 31 adjusting entry?
options: Debit Insurance Expense $1,000; Credit Prepaid Insurance $1,000
questions.explain: Each month, 1/12 of the prepaid amount ($1,000) is moved from the Prepaid Insurance asset into Insurance Expense as it is actually used.

questions.q: Which Oracle Fusion capability was described as cleaning up many accrual-side adjustments automatically?
options: The reversing-entry feature in General Ledger
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion General Ledger's reversing-entry feature, introduced in lesson 15, is the mechanism that cleans up many accrual-side adjustments once the real transaction occurs.
